Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 969 of 2021

Revisionist :- X-Juvenile
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.And Another

Counsel for Revisionist :- Ajay Kumar Jagdish,Braham Vishal Nayak
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ram Manohar Narayan Mishra,J.
1.

Learned counsel for the revisionist has made oral prayer to incorporate the amendment in array of parties in memo of criminal revision, pursuant to order order dated 09.05.2023 passed by this Court as due to inadvertance the name of Juvenile could not be deleted in memo of revision.
2. Prayer so made is allowed.
3. Let amendment be incorporated as prayed forthwith.

4. As per office report dated 04.08.2021, notice issued to respondent no. 2 has been served upon her personally, but none appeared on her behalf to contest the present revision and counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of respondent no. 1-State of U.P.
5.
Heard learned counsel for the revisionist and learned A.G.A. for the State.

Ait District- Jalaun

sentences.text: has been dismissed.

The revisionist has assailed the appellate order dated 30.11.2020 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge/ Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Jalaun in Criminal Appeal No.
02 of 2020 whereby the appeal preferred against the said bail rejection of J.J.B. has been dismissed and consequently, the order dated 06.03.2020 of J.J.B, Meerut has been affirmed.
7.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge/ Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Jalaun
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that the revisionist is held in custody of Government Observation Home since 06.12.2019 in said case.

According to prosecution version the revisionist committed rape on five months old daughter of the informant on 12.06.2019 at around 09:30 hours by taking her to nearby shrubs on pretext on providing her some eatable.
She was found in blood stained condition by the informant.
He next submitted that revisionist is falsely implicated in the case.
The allegations against the revisionist are not natural.
This is settled law that bail cannot be denied to a juvenile solely on the basis of gravity of allegations against him.

8. The provision for grant of denial of bail to juvenile, who is in conflict with law is provided under Section 12 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection) Act-2015 which is provided as under:-
"(1) When any person, who is apparently a child and is alleged to have committed a bailable or non - bailable offence, is apprehended or detained by the police or appears or brought before a Board, such person shall, notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974) or in any other law for the time being in force, be released on bail with or without surety or placed under the supervision of a probation officer or under the care of any fit person:

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection) Act-2015 which
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Provided that such person shall not be so released if there appears reasonable grounds for believing that the release is likely to bring that person into association with any known criminal or expose the said person to moral, physical or psychological danger or the persons release would defeat the ends of justice, and the Board shall record the reasons for denying the bail and circumstances that led to such a decision.

(2) When such person having been apprehended is not released on bail under sub - section (1) by the officer - in - charge of the police station, such officer shall cause the person to be kept only in an observation home or a place of safety, as the case may be in such manner as may be prescribed until the person can be brought before a Board.

(3) When such person is not released on bail under sub - section (1) by the Board, it shall make an order sending him to an observation home or a place of safety, as the case may be, for such period during the pendency of the inquiry regarding the person,
as may be specified in the order.

(4) When a child in conflict with law is unable to fulfil the conditions of bail order within seven days of the bail order, such child shall be produced before the Board for X-Juvenile vs State Of U.P.And Another on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23556922/
2 modification of the conditions of bail."
9.

entities.text: X-Juvenile vs State Of U.P.And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He next submitted that both the courts below have committed legal and factual error while dismissing the prayer for bail made on behalf of the revisionist.
The revisionist is not a previous convict, he has no criminal antecedents and he is not a habitual offender.
There is nothing adverse against the revisionist in the report of District Probation Officer filed on 06.12.2019 with regard to the revisionist.
There is no material as such by courts below for their satisfaction regarding fulfillment of conditions of bail as provided under Section 12 of the Act for denial of the bail to juvenile.
The revisionist has been held in custody of observation home for a period of more than four years.
Thus, he has undergone more than three years of custody as provided under Section 18 of the Act.
The trial is in progress and three witnesses have been examined before the trial court.
10. Per contra, learned A.G.A. submitted that the offence is of heinous nature where the revisionist is sole accused, who has committed rape on five months old child.
The nature and mode of commission of offence is such that in case of grant of bail to the juvenile, the ends of justice will get defeated.

11. In social investigation report dated 10.02.2020, District Probation Officer, Hamirpur has stated that from people of locality the complicity of the revisionist was not established as he has reportedly visited the place of his aunt on the fateful day, it is further stated that he has received education upto Class VIII and economic condition of his mother is not good, therefore, he is not able to continue his education.
The healthy and congenial atmosphere is liable to be provided to the child.
12. From the perusal of record, it also appears that revisionist is distant relative of the victim and no plausible reasons have surfaced to suggest his false implications in the case.
The trial is in progress.

13. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the heinous nature of the offence allegedly committed by the revisionist, wherein five months old child has been been allegedly subjected to rape, I am of the considered opinion that in case of grant of bail the ends of justice will be defeated.
14. This Court is not inclined to grant release of bail to juvenile at this stage.
Accordingly, the revision is dismissed.

15. However, keeping in view the fact that the revisionist is held in jail custody for more than four years in this case, the trial court is directed to expedite the trial of the case and decide the same preferably within period of six months after giving opportunity of hearing to the parties concerned and without granting unnecessary adjournments to either of the parties provided there is no other legal impediment.

Order Date :- 16.4.2024 Nitika Sri.
